title: catalog-delta-propagation-and-signed-rollback-playbook
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Problem: Publishing Redwood-verified perf profiles currently pushes changes to the catalog with limited propagation controls. When a perf delta (latency/throughput/cost) slips through verification, customers pinned to a model variant can see regressions before we react. Goal: introduce a signed manifest + propagation window approach that makes profile publishes auditable, staged (regional/canary), and automatically reversible when telemetry indicates regressions. This ticket scopes the publish workflow changes, console UX for propagation controls, rollback playbook, and the telemetry signals and thresholds that trigger automated or semi-automated rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Publish pipeline emits a signed manifest (git-backed SHA + signature) per profile publish
Console UI exposes propagation controls: scope (global/regional), rollout speed (immediate/24h/72h), and canary percentage
Catalog propagation honors manifest scope and only promotes to higher percentages after heuristics pass
Automatic rollback trigger defined and implemented: if latency regression > 5 p95 relative to baseline OR error rate > 0.5% sustained for 15m, manifest rollback is initiated
Rollback operates at the same granularity as the rollout scope (region/route/customer tier) and records an audit event with signed revert manifest
Telemetry dashboards show cohorted metrics (canary vs baseline), and an alert runbook exists with Slack + PagerDuty playbook
E2E tests for manifest signing, propagation, and rollback added to onboarding test harness
Documentation (Confluence) and Console help copy updated with a short video walkthrough

decisions: Use git-backed manifests (catalog repo) signed by the publish service to provide non-repudiable provenance
Manifests include: model_id, exact model_version, runtime-compatibility-tag, kernel-hint, quantization-profile, cost-fingerprint, propagation-policy
Default propagation window set to 24h with two-step canary (1% -> 10%) unless overridden by profile owner
Rollback policy: automated triggers for high-severity regressions, manual rollback for low-confidence signals
Cost normalization uses baseline instance equivalent (vCPU/GPU t-coeff) to report cost-per-token normalized to the canonical hardware family
open_questions: Should rollback playbook allow auto-redeploy of previous manifest only, or also swap to a compatible variant (smaller quantized model) as a fallback?
What are exact thresholds per model class (chat vs completion vs embeddings)? Proposal: start with uniform thresholds and tune post-canary
How granular should propagation scope be for enterprise customers with dedicated capacity? (tenant-level vs region-level)
Do we display the signed manifest contents in Console or only metadata and signature? Security team prefers metadata + verify button
Edge case: how to reconcile concurrent publishes that touch the same variant key during a propagation window?
